source_blocks.html: Install Streamlit using command line

This page will walk you through creating an environment with venv and installing Streamlit with pip. These are our recommended tools, but if you are familiar with others you can use your favorite ones too. At the end, you'll build a simple "Hello world" app and run it. If you prefer to have a graphical interface to manage your Python environments, check out how to Install Streamlit using Anaconda Distribution.
Prerequisites
As with any programming tool, in order to install Streamlit you first need to make sure your computer is properly set up. More specifically, you’ll need:

1. Python

    We support version 3.11 to 3.15.

  2. A Python environment manager (recommended)

    Environment managers create virtual environments to isolate Python package installations between projects.

    We recommend using virtual environments because installing or upgrading a Python package may cause unintentional effects on another package. For a detailed introduction to Python environments, check out Python Virtual Environments: A Primer.

    For this guide, we'll be using venv, which comes with Python.

  3. A Python package manager

    Package managers handle installing each of your Python packages, including Streamlit.

    For this guide, we'll be using pip, which comes with Python.

  4. Only on MacOS: Xcode command line tools

    Download Xcode command line tools using these instructions in order to let the package manager install some of Streamlit's dependencies.

  5. A code editor

    Our favorite editor is VS Code, which is also what we use in all our tutorials.
Create an environment using venv

1. Open a terminal and navigate to your project folder.

    Terminal
    cd myproject

  2. In your terminal, type:

    Terminal
    python -m venv .venv

  3. A folder named ".venv" will appear in your project. This directory is where your virtual environment and its dependencies are installed.
Activate your environment

1. In your terminal, activate your environment with one of the following commands, depending on your operating system.

    Terminal
    # Windows command prompt
.venv\Scripts\activate.bat

# Windows PowerShell
.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1

# macOS and Linux
source .venv/bin/activate

  2. Once activated, you will see your environment name in parentheses before your prompt. "(.venv)"
Install Streamlit in your environment

1. In the terminal with your environment activated, type:

    Terminal
    pip install streamlit

  2. Test that the installation worked by launching the Streamlit Hello example app:

    Terminal
    streamlit hello

    If this doesn't work, use the long-form command:

    Terminal
    python -m streamlit hello

  3. Streamlit's Hello app should appear in a new tab in your web browser!

    Interactive demo (opens online)
    Built with Streamlit 🎈
    Fullscreen open_in_new

star

Tip

If you use an AI coding agent, install Streamlit's official agent skills so it follows current Streamlit APIs:

Terminal
streamlit skills

For details, see streamlit skills.
1. Close your terminal when you are done.
Create a "Hello World" app and run it
1. Create a file named app.py in your project folder.

Python
import streamlit as st

st.write("Hello world")
1. Any time you want to use your new environment, you first need to go to your project folder (where the .venv directory lives) and run the command to activate it:

Terminal
# Windows command prompt
.venv\Scripts\activate.bat

# Windows PowerShell
.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1

# macOS and Linux
source .venv/bin/activate

1. Once activated, you will see your environment's name in parentheses at the beginning of your terminal prompt. "(.venv)"

  2. Run your Streamlit app.

Terminal
streamlit run app.py
If this doesn't work, use the long-form command:

Terminal
python -m streamlit run app.py

1. To stop the Streamlit server, press Ctrl+C in the terminal.

  2. When you're done using this environment, return to your normal shell by typing:

Terminal
deactivate

blocks.html: 通过命令行安装 Streamlit
本页将带你使用 venv 创建环境，并通过 pip 安装 Streamlit。这些是我们推荐的工具；如果你熟悉其他工具，也可以选择自己喜欢的方式。最后，你将构建并运行一个简单的“Hello world”应用。如果更喜欢通过图形界面管理 Python 环境，可以了解如何使用 Anaconda Distribution 安装 Streamlit.
前置条件
和使用其他编程工具一样，安装 Streamlit 前需要先准备好电脑。具体来说，你需要：

1. Python

    我们支持 3.11 至 3.15 版本.

  2. Python 环境管理器（推荐）

    环境管理器会创建虚拟环境，让不同项目安装的 Python 软件包彼此隔离。

    我们推荐使用虚拟环境，因为安装或升级某个 Python 包，可能会意外影响另一个包。关于 Python 环境的详细介绍，请阅读Python 虚拟环境入门.

    本指南使用 venv，它随 Python 一起提供。

  3. Python 包管理器

    包管理器负责安装各个 Python 软件包，包括 Streamlit。

    本指南使用 pip，它随 Python 一起提供。

  4. 仅 macOS 需要：Xcode 命令行工具

    请按照这些说明下载 Xcode 命令行工具，让包管理器能够安装 Streamlit 的部分依赖。

  5. 代码编辑器

    我们喜欢的编辑器是 VS Code，本套教程也都使用它。
使用下列工具创建环境：venv

1. 打开终端，进入项目文件夹。

    终端
    cd myproject

  2. 在终端中输入：

    终端
    python -m venv .venv

  3. 项目中会出现一个名为“.venv”的文件夹，虚拟环境及其依赖将安装在该目录中。
激活环境

1. 根据所用操作系统，在终端中使用以下相应命令激活环境。

    终端
    # Windows command prompt
.venv\Scripts\activate.bat

# Windows PowerShell
.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1

# macOS and Linux
source .venv/bin/activate

  2. 激活后，命令提示符前会以括号显示环境名：“(.venv)”。
在环境中安装 Streamlit

1. 在已激活环境的终端中输入：

    终端
    pip install streamlit

  2. 启动 Streamlit Hello 示例应用，检查安装是否成功：

    终端
    streamlit hello

    如果该命令无法使用，请尝试完整的模块调用形式：

    终端
    python -m streamlit hello

  3. Streamlit Hello 应用应当会出现在浏览器的新标签页中！

cards.title: 重新运行：为什么点一下，代码又执行了？
cards.summary: 默认的数据流可以理解为：交互组件（widget）的值变化时，Streamlit 会重新从上到下执行脚本，再按最新输入刷新界面。
cards.when_to_use: 页面上有滑块、输入框或按钮，需要理解更新顺序时。
steps: 按从上到下的顺序组织代码。
把组件返回的值交给后面的计算和显示语句。
修改源码并保存后，可以按页面提示重新运行，开发时也可开启自动重新运行。
notes: 这里解释默认整页运行方式；进阶的表单和局部重运行有各自规则。

cards.title: 把用户输入当作 Python 变量
cards.summary: 滑块、复选框和下拉框会提供当前输入值。把返回值保存到变量，就能用平常的 Python 判断和计算控制页面。
cards.when_to_use: 需要选择筛选条件，或让用户决定是否显示一块内容时。
steps: 选择合适的输入组件，设置清楚的标签。
接住组件返回值，例如复选框返回的布尔值。
在后面的 if 判断中使用它，控制显示内容。

source_blocks.html: Basic concepts of Streamlit
Working with Streamlit is simple. First you sprinkle a few Streamlit commands into a normal Python script, then you run it with streamlit run:

Terminal
streamlit run your_script.py [-- script args]

As soon as you run the script as shown above, a local Streamlit server will spin up and your app will open in a new tab in your default web browser. The app is your canvas, where you'll draw charts, text, widgets, tables, and more.

What gets drawn in the app is up to you. For example st.text writes raw text to your app, and st.line_chart draws — you guessed it — a line chart. Refer to our API documentation to see all commands that are available to you.

push_pin

Note

When passing your script some custom arguments, they must be passed after two dashes. Otherwise the arguments get interpreted as arguments to Streamlit itself.
Another way of running Streamlit is to run it as a Python module. This can be useful when configuring an IDE like PyCharm to work with Streamlit:

Terminal
# Running
python -m streamlit run your_script.py

# is equivalent to:
streamlit run your_script.py

star

Tip

You can also pass a URL to streamlit run! This is great when combined with GitHub Gists. For example:

Terminal
streamlit run https://raw.githubusercontent.com/streamlit/demo-uber-nyc-pickups/master/streamlit_app.py
Development flow

Every time you want to update your app, save the source file. When you do that, Streamlit detects if there is a change and asks you whether you want to rerun your app. Choose "Always rerun" at the top-right of your screen to automatically update your app every time you change its source code.

This allows you to work in a fast interactive loop: you type some code, save it, try it out live, then type some more code, save it, try it out, and so on until you're happy with the results. This tight loop between coding and viewing results live is one of the ways Streamlit makes your life easier.

star

Tip

While developing a Streamlit app, it's recommended to lay out your editor and browser windows side by side, so the code and the app can be seen at the same time. Give it a try!

As of Streamlit version 1.10.0 and higher, Streamlit apps cannot be run from the root directory of Linux distributions. If you try to run a Streamlit app from the root directory, Streamlit will throw a FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory error. For more information, see GitHub issue #5239.

If you are using Streamlit version 1.10.0 or higher, your main script should live in a directory other than the root directory. When using Docker, you can use the WORKDIR command to specify the directory where your main script lives. For an example of how to do this, read Create a Dockerfile.
Data flow

Streamlit's architecture allows you to write apps the same way you write plain Python scripts. To unlock this, Streamlit apps have a unique data flow: any time something must be updated on the screen, Streamlit reruns your entire Python script from top to bottom.
This can happen in two situations:

• Whenever you modify your app's source code.

  • Whenever a user interacts with widgets in the app. For example, when dragging a slider, entering text in an input box, or clicking a button.

Whenever a callback is passed to a widget via the on_change (or on_click) parameter, the callback will always run before the rest of your script. For details on the Callbacks API, please refer to our Session State API Reference Guide.

And to make all of this fast and seamless, Streamlit does some heavy lifting for you behind the scenes. A big player in this story is the @st.cache_data decorator, which allows developers to skip certain costly computations when their apps rerun. Caching is covered in more detail in Advanced concepts.
Display and style data

There are a few ways to display data (tables, arrays, data frames) in Streamlit apps. Below, you will be introduced to magic and st.write(), which can be used to write anything from text to tables. After that, let's take a look at methods designed specifically for visualizing data.
Use magic
You can also write to your app without calling any Streamlit methods. Streamlit supports "magic commands," which means you don't have to use st.write() at all! To see this in action try this snippet:

Python
"""
# My first app
Here's our first attempt at using data to create a table:
"""

import streamlit as st
import pandas as pd
df = pd.DataFrame({
  'first column': [1, 2, 3, 4],
  'second column': [10, 20, 30, 40]
})

df

Any time that Streamlit sees a variable or a literal value on its own line, it automatically writes that to your app using st.write(). For more information, refer to the documentation on magic commands.
Write a data frame

Along with magic commands, st.write() is Streamlit's "Swiss Army knife". You can pass almost anything to st.write(): text, data, Matplotlib figures, Altair charts, and more. Don't worry, Streamlit will figure it out and render things the right way.

Python
import streamlit as st
import pandas as pd

st.write("Here's our first attempt at using data to create a table:")
st.write(pd.DataFrame({
    'first column': [1, 2, 3, 4],
    'second column': [10, 20, 30, 40]
}))

There are other data specific functions like st.dataframe() and st.table() that you can also use for displaying data. Let's understand when to use these features and how to add colors and styling to your data frames.
You might be asking yourself, "why wouldn't I always use st.write()?" There are a few reasons:

1. Magic and st.write() inspect the type of data that you've passed in, and then decide how to best render it in the app. Sometimes you want to draw it another way. For example, instead of drawing a dataframe as an interactive table, you may want to draw it as a static table by using st.table(df).
  2. The second reason is that other methods return an object that can be used and modified, either by adding data to it or replacing it.
  3. Finally, if you use a more specific Streamlit method you can pass additional arguments to customize its behavior.

For example, let's create a data frame and change its formatting with a Pandas Styler object. In this example, you'll use Numpy to generate a random sample, and the st.dataframe() method to draw an interactive table.

push_pin

Note

This example uses Numpy to generate a random sample, but you can use Pandas DataFrames, Numpy arrays, or plain Python arrays.

Python
import streamlit as st
import numpy as np

dataframe = np.random.randn(10, 20)
st.dataframe(dataframe)
Let's expand on the first example using the Pandas Styler object to highlight some elements in the interactive table.

Python
import streamlit as st
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

dataframe = pd.DataFrame(
    np.random.randn(10, 20),
    columns=('col %d' % i for i in range(20)))

st.dataframe(dataframe.style.highlight_max(axis=0))
Streamlit also has a method for static table generation: st.table().

Python
import streamlit as st
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

dataframe = pd.DataFrame(
    np.random.randn(10, 20),
    columns=('col %d' % i for i in range(20)))
st.table(dataframe)
Draw charts and maps
Streamlit supports several popular data charting libraries like Matplotlib, Altair, deck.gl, and more. In this section, you'll add a bar chart, line chart, and a map to your app.
Draw a line chart
You can easily add a line chart to your app with st.line_chart(). We'll generate a random sample using Numpy and then chart it.

Python
import streamlit as st
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

chart_data = pd.DataFrame(
     np.random.randn(20, 3),
     columns=['a', 'b', 'c'])

st.line_chart(chart_data)
Plot a map
With st.map() you can display data points on a map. Let's use Numpy to generate some sample data and plot it on a map of San Francisco.

Python
import streamlit as st
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

map_data = pd.DataFrame(
    np.random.randn(1000, 2) / [50, 50] + [37.76, -122.4],
    columns=['lat', 'lon'])

st.map(map_data)
Widgets

When you've got the data or model into the state that you want to explore, you can add in widgets like st.slider(), st.button() or st.selectbox(). It's really straightforward — treat widgets as variables:

Python
import streamlit as st
x = st.slider('x')  # 👈 this is a widget
st.write(x, 'squared is', x * x)

On first run, the app above should output the text "0 squared is 0". Then every time a user interacts with a widget, Streamlit simply reruns your script from top to bottom, assigning the current state of the widget to your variable in the process.
For example, if the user moves the slider to position 10, Streamlit will rerun the code above and set x to 10 accordingly. So now you should see the text "10 squared is 100".
Widgets can also be accessed by key, if you choose to specify a string to use as the unique key for the widget:

Python
import streamlit as st
st.text_input("Your name", key="name")

# You can access the value at any point with:
st.session_state.name

Every widget with a key is automatically added to Session State. For more information about Session State, its association with widget state, and its limitations, see Session State API Reference Guide.
Use checkboxes to show/hide data

One use case for checkboxes is to hide or show a specific chart or section in an app. st.checkbox() takes a single argument, which is the widget label. In this sample, the checkbox is used to toggle a conditional statement.

Python
import streamlit as st
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

if st.checkbox('Show dataframe'):
    chart_data = pd.DataFrame(
       np.random.randn(20, 3),
       columns=['a', 'b', 'c'])

    chart_data
Use a selectbox for options
Use st.selectbox to choose from a series. You can write in the options you want, or pass through an array or data frame column.
Let's use the df data frame we created earlier.

Python
import streamlit as st
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({
    'first column': [1, 2, 3, 4],
    'second column': [10, 20, 30, 40]
    })

option = st.selectbox(
    'Which number do you like best?',
     df['first column'])

'You selected: ', option
Layout

Streamlit makes it easy to organize your widgets in a left panel sidebar with st.sidebar. Each element that's passed to st.sidebar is pinned to the left, allowing users to focus on the content in your app while still having access to UI controls.
For example, if you want to add a selectbox and a slider to a sidebar, use st.sidebar.slider and st.sidebar.selectbox instead of st.slider and st.selectbox:

Python
import streamlit as st

# Add a selectbox to the sidebar:
add_selectbox = st.sidebar.selectbox(
    'How would you like to be contacted?',
    ('Email', 'Home phone', 'Mobile phone')
)

# Add a slider to the sidebar:
add_slider = st.sidebar.slider(
    'Select a range of values',
    0.0, 100.0, (25.0, 75.0)
)

Beyond the sidebar, Streamlit offers several other ways to control the layout of your app. st.columns lets you place widgets side-by-side, and st.expander lets you conserve space by hiding away large content.

Python
import streamlit as st

left_column, right_column = st.columns(2)
# You can use a column just like st.sidebar:
left_column.button('Press me!')

# Or even better, call Streamlit functions inside a "with" block:
with right_column:
    chosen = st.radio(
        'Sorting hat',
        ("Gryffindor", "Ravenclaw", "Hufflepuff", "Slytherin"))
    st.write(f"You are in {chosen} house!")

push_pin

Note

st.echo and st.spinner are not currently supported inside the sidebar or layout options. Rest assured, though, we're currently working on adding support for those too!
Show progress
When adding long running computations to an app, you can use st.progress() to display status in real time.
First, let's import time. We're going to use the time.sleep() method to simulate a long running computation:

Python
import time
Now, let's create a progress bar:

Python
import streamlit as st
import time

'Starting a long computation...'

# Add a placeholder
latest_iteration = st.empty()
bar = st.progress(0)

for i in range(100):
  # Update the progress bar with each iteration.
  latest_iteration.text(f'Iteration {i+1}')
  bar.progress(i + 1)
  time.sleep(0.1)

'...and now we\'re done!'

blocks.html: Streamlit 基础概念
使用 Streamlit 很简单。先在普通的 Python 脚本中加入几个 Streamlit 命令，再用以下命令运行：streamlit run:

终端
streamlit run your_script.py [-- script args]
按上面的方式运行脚本后，本地 Streamlit 服务就会启动，应用会在默认浏览器的新标签页中打开。应用就是你的画布，可以在其中绘制图表、文本、交互组件、表格等内容。
页面具体展示什么，由你决定。例如，st.text可以向应用写入原始文本，而 st.line_chart顾名思义，会绘制折线图。请查阅API 文档，了解所有可用命令。

●

说明

向脚本传递自定义参数时，参数必须放在两个连字符之后；否则，它们会被当作 Streamlit 自身的参数。
还可以把 Streamlit 当作 Python 模块运行。在配置 PyCharm 等 IDE 时，这种方式可能很有用：

终端
# Running
python -m streamlit run your_script.py

# is equivalent to:
streamlit run your_script.py

★

提示

你也可以向 streamlit run 传入 URL！与 GitHub Gists 配合使用尤其方便。例如：

终端
streamlit run https://raw.githubusercontent.com/streamlit/demo-uber-nyc-pickups/master/streamlit_app.py
开发流程
每次需要更新应用时，请保存源文件。Streamlit 会检测变化，并询问是否重新运行应用。选择屏幕右上方的“Always rerun”（始终重新运行），之后每次修改源码时就会自动更新应用。
这样就能形成快速的交互式开发循环：写代码、保存、实时试用，再继续写一些代码、保存、试用，直到对结果满意。编码与查看结果之间的紧密循环，是 Streamlit 简化开发体验的方式之一。

★

提示

开发 Streamlit 应用时，推荐将编辑器和浏览器并排摆放，方便同时查看代码与应用。不妨试试看！
从 Streamlit 1.10.0 开始，应用不能从 Linux 发行版的根目录启动。如果这样运行，Streamlit 会抛出 FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory 错误。更多信息请参阅 GitHub 问题 #5239.
如果使用 Streamlit 1.10.0 或更新版本，请将主脚本放在根目录以外的目录中。在 Docker 中，可以使用 WORKDIR 命令指定主脚本所在目录。示例请参阅创建 Dockerfile.
数据流
Streamlit 的架构允许你像编写普通 Python 脚本一样编写应用。为了做到这一点，它采用了独特的数据流：屏幕上的内容每当需要更新，Streamlit 就会把整个 Python 脚本从上到下重新运行。
这种情况可能在以下两种情形中发生：

• 修改应用源代码时。

  • 用户与应用中的交互组件发生交互时，例如拖动滑块、在输入框中输入文本，或点击按钮。
通过交互组件的 on_change（或 on_click）参数传入回调函数时，回调总会先于脚本的其余部分运行。回调 API 的详细说明，请参阅会话状态 API 参考指南.
为了让这一切快速、顺畅地完成，Streamlit 会在后台承担许多复杂工作。其中一个重要角色是 @st.cache_data 装饰器，它使应用重新运行时能够跳过某些代价较高的计算。进阶概念中会更详细地介绍缓存。
展示数据与设置样式
Streamlit 提供多种方式展示表格、数组和数据表。下面将介绍 自动显示和 st.write()，它们能够输出文本、表格等多种内容。之后，我们再看看专门用于数据可视化的方法。
使用自动显示功能
即使不调用 Streamlit 的方法，也能向应用输出内容。Streamlit 支持“自动显示命令”，因此完全不必调用 st.write()！试试下面的代码，就能看到效果：

Python
"""
# My first app
Here's our first attempt at using data to create a table:
"""

import streamlit as st
import pandas as pd
df = pd.DataFrame({
  'first column': [1, 2, 3, 4],
  'second column': [10, 20, 30, 40]
})

df
只要 Streamlit 看到某个变量或字面量独占一行，就会自动使用 st.write() 将它显示在应用中。更多信息请参阅自动显示命令.
显示数据表
与 自动显示命令, st.write() 是 Streamlit 的“瑞士军刀”。你几乎可以向 st.write() 传入任何内容：文本、数据、Matplotlib 图形、Altair 图表等等。不必担心，Streamlit 会判断并正确渲染。

Python
import streamlit as st
import pandas as pd

st.write("Here's our first attempt at using data to create a table:")
st.write(pd.DataFrame({
    'first column': [1, 2, 3, 4],
    'second column': [10, 20, 30, 40]
}))
你也可以使用其他面向特定数据的函数，例如 st.dataframe() 和 st.table()，来展示数据。下面我们了解这些功能分别适用于什么情况，以及如何为数据表添加颜色和样式。
你可能会问：“为什么不一直使用 st.write()？”原因有以下几个：

1. 自动显示和 st.write() 会检查传入的数据类型，并决定合适的渲染方式。但有时，你希望换一种方式展示。例如，不想把数据表显示成交互式表格，而是希望使用 st.table(df).
  2. 第二个原因是，其他方法会返回一个对象，你可以继续添加数据或替换数据，修改它的内容。
  3. 最后，使用更具体的 Streamlit 方法时，还可以传入额外参数，自定义其行为。
例如，我们来创建一个数据表，并用 Pandas 的 Styler 对象修改其格式。本示例将用 NumPy 生成随机样本，再通过 st.dataframe() 方法绘制交互式表格。

●

说明

本示例用 NumPy 生成随机样本，但也可以使用 Pandas 数据表、NumPy 数组或普通 Python 数组。

Python
import streamlit as st
import numpy as np

dataframe = np.random.randn(10, 20)
st.dataframe(dataframe)
接下来扩展第一个示例，使用 Pandas 的 Styler 对象突出显示交互式表格中的某些元素。

Python
import streamlit as st
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

dataframe = pd.DataFrame(
    np.random.randn(10, 20),
    columns=('col %d' % i for i in range(20)))

st.dataframe(dataframe.style.highlight_max(axis=0))
Streamlit 也提供生成静态表格的方法：st.table().

Python
import streamlit as st
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

dataframe = pd.DataFrame(
    np.random.randn(10, 20),
    columns=('col %d' % i for i in range(20)))
st.table(dataframe)
绘制图表与地图
Streamlit 支持多种常用的数据图表库，例如 Matplotlib、Altair、deck.gl 等。本节会向应用添加柱状图、折线图和地图。
绘制折线图
使用 st.line_chart() 就能轻松为应用添加折线图。我们用 NumPy 生成随机样本，再将其绘制出来。

Python
import streamlit as st
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

chart_data = pd.DataFrame(
     np.random.randn(20, 3),
     columns=['a', 'b', 'c'])

st.line_chart(chart_data)
绘制地图
使用 st.map() 可以在地图上显示数据点。下面用 NumPy 生成一些样本数据，并将它们绘制在旧金山的地图上。

Python
import streamlit as st
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

map_data = pd.DataFrame(
    np.random.randn(1000, 2) / [50, 50] + [37.76, -122.4],
    columns=['lat', 'lon'])

st.map(map_data)
交互组件
准备好要探索的数据或模型后，就可以加入交互组件，例如 st.slider(), st.button() 或 st.selectbox()。方法很直接：把交互组件当作变量使用。

Python
import streamlit as st
x = st.slider('x')  # 👈 this is a widget
st.write(x, 'squared is', x * x)
首次运行时，上面的应用应输出“0 squared is 0”。之后，每次用户操作交互组件时，Streamlit 都会从上到下重新运行脚本，并把组件当前状态赋给相应变量。
例如，用户把滑块移动到 10 时，Streamlit 会重新运行上面的代码，并将 x 设置为 10。因此，此时应当看到“10 squared is 100”。
如果为交互组件指定了唯一字符串 key，也可以通过 key 访问它：

Python
import streamlit as st
st.text_input("Your name", key="name")

# You can access the value at any point with:
st.session_state.name
每个设置了 key 的交互组件，都会自动加入会话状态。有关会话状态、它与组件状态的关系及其限制，请参阅会话状态 API 参考指南.
使用复选框显示或隐藏数据
复选框的一种用途，是显示或隐藏应用中的某张图表或某个部分。st.checkbox() 接收一个参数作为组件标签。此示例通过复选框控制条件语句。

Python
import streamlit as st
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

if st.checkbox('Show dataframe'):
    chart_data = pd.DataFrame(
       np.random.randn(20, 3),
       columns=['a', 'b', 'c'])

    chart_data
使用下拉框选择选项
使用 st.selectbox 可以从一组值中选择。你可以直接写出想要的选项，也可以传入数组或数据表中的一列。
下面使用前面创建的 df 数据表。

Python
import streamlit as st
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({
    'first column': [1, 2, 3, 4],
    'second column': [10, 20, 30, 40]
    })

option = st.selectbox(
    'Which number do you like best?',
     df['first column'])

'You selected: ', option
布局
使用 st.sidebar，可以轻松把交互组件放入左侧侧边栏。传给 st.sidebar 的每个元素都会固定在左侧，让用户在仍可使用控制项的同时，专注于应用的主要内容。
例如，要把下拉框和滑块放在侧边栏中，请使用 st.sidebar.slider和 st.sidebar.selectbox，代替 st.slider 和 st.selectbox:

Python
import streamlit as st

# Add a selectbox to the sidebar:
add_selectbox = st.sidebar.selectbox(
    'How would you like to be contacted?',
    ('Email', 'Home phone', 'Mobile phone')
)

# Add a slider to the sidebar:
add_slider = st.sidebar.slider(
    'Select a range of values',
    0.0, 100.0, (25.0, 75.0)
)
除了侧边栏，Streamlit 还有其他几种控制应用布局的方式。st.columns 可以把交互组件并排放置，而 st.expander 可以折叠大段内容，从而节省空间。

Python
import streamlit as st

left_column, right_column = st.columns(2)
# You can use a column just like st.sidebar:
left_column.button('Press me!')

# Or even better, call Streamlit functions inside a "with" block:
with right_column:
    chosen = st.radio(
        'Sorting hat',
        ("Gryffindor", "Ravenclaw", "Hufflepuff", "Slytherin"))
    st.write(f"You are in {chosen} house!")

●

说明

st.echo和 st.spinner 目前尚不支持放在侧边栏或布局选项中。我们正在努力增加这些支持，敬请放心！
显示进度
给应用加入耗时计算时，可以使用 st.progress() 实时显示状态。
先导入 time。我们将用 time.sleep() 方法模拟耗时计算：

Python
import time
现在创建一个进度条：

Python
import streamlit as st
import time

'Starting a long computation...'

# Add a placeholder
latest_iteration = st.empty()
bar = st.progress(0)

for i in range(100):
  # Update the progress bar with each iteration.
  latest_iteration.text(f'Iteration {i+1}')
  bar.progress(i + 1)
  time.sleep(0.1)

'...and now we\'re done!'

cards.summary: 缓存（cache）会保存函数结果。官方教程把 st.cache_data 放在数据加载函数上，减少应用重新运行时重复下载和处理相同数据。
cards.when_to_use: 读文件、下载数据或计算较慢，且希望复用结果时。
steps: 把需要复用结果的工作整理成函数。

在页面中像调用普通函数一样调用它。

steps: 先准备带小时和数值的示例数据。
用 st.slider 得到选中的小时。
用这个值筛选数据，再把结果交给展示函数。

source_blocks.html: Create an app
If you've made it this far, chances are you've installed Streamlit and run through the basics in Basic concepts and Advanced concepts. If not, now is a good time to take a look.

The easiest way to learn how to use Streamlit is to try things out yourself. As you read through this guide, test each method. As long as your app is running, every time you add a new element to your script and save, Streamlit's UI will ask if you'd like to rerun the app and view the changes. This allows you to work in a fast interactive loop: you write some code, save it, review the output, write some more, and so on, until you're happy with the results. The goal is to use Streamlit to create an interactive app for your data or model and along the way to use Streamlit to review, debug, perfect, and share your code.

In this guide, you're going to use Streamlit's core features to create an interactive app; exploring a public Uber dataset for pickups and drop-offs in New York City. When you're finished, you'll know how to fetch and cache data, draw charts, plot information on a map, and use interactive widgets, like a slider, to filter results.

star

Tip

If you'd like to skip ahead and see everything at once, the complete script is available below.
Create your first app

Streamlit is more than just a way to make data apps, it’s also a community of creators that share their apps and ideas and help each other make their work better. Please come join us on the community forum. We love to hear your questions, ideas, and help you work through your bugs — stop by today!

1. The first step is to create a new Python script. Let's call it uber_pickups.py.

  2. Open uber_pickups.py in your favorite IDE or text editor, then add these lines:

    Python
    import streamlit as st
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

  3. Every good app has a title, so let's add one:

    Python
    st.title('Uber pickups in NYC')

  4. Now it's time to run Streamlit from the command line:

    Terminal
    streamlit run uber_pickups.py

    Running a Streamlit app is no different than any other Python script. Whenever you need to view the app, you can use this command.

    star

    Tip

    Did you know you can also pass a URL to streamlit run? This is great when combined with GitHub Gists. For example:

    Terminal
    streamlit run https://raw.githubusercontent.com/streamlit/demo-uber-nyc-pickups/master/streamlit_app.py

  5. As usual, the app should automatically open in a new tab in your browser.
Fetch some data
Now that you have an app, the next thing you'll need to do is fetch the Uber dataset for pickups and drop-offs in New York City.

1. Let's start by writing a function to load the data. Add this code to your script:

    Python
    DATE_COLUMN = 'date/time'
DATA_URL = ('https://s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com/'
         'streamlit-demo-data/uber-raw-data-sep14.csv.gz')

def load_data(nrows):
    data = pd.read_csv(DATA_URL, nrows=nrows)
    lowercase = lambda x: str(x).lower()
    data.rename(lowercase, axis='columns', inplace=True)
    data[DATE_COLUMN] = pd.to_datetime(data[DATE_COLUMN])
    return data

    You'll notice that load_data is a plain old function that downloads some data, puts it in a Pandas dataframe, and converts the date column from text to datetime. The function accepts a single parameter (nrows), which specifies the number of rows that you want to load into the dataframe.

  2. Now let's test the function and review the output. Below your function, add these lines:

    Python
    # Create a text element and let the reader know the data is loading.
data_load_state = st.text('Loading data...')
# Load 10,000 rows of data into the dataframe.
data = load_data(10000)
# Notify the reader that the data was successfully loaded.
data_load_state.text('Loading data...done!')

    You'll see a few buttons in the upper-right corner of your app asking if you'd like to rerun the app. Choose Always rerun, and you'll see your changes automatically each time you save.
Ok, that's underwhelming...

It turns out that it takes a long time to download data, and load 10,000 lines into a dataframe. Converting the date column into datetime isn’t a quick job either. You don’t want to reload the data each time the app is updated – luckily Streamlit allows you to cache the data.
Effortless caching

1. Try adding @st.cache_data before the load_data declaration:

    Python
    @st.cache_data
def load_data(nrows):

  2. Then save the script, and Streamlit will automatically rerun your app. Since this is the first time you’re running the script with @st.cache_data, you won't see anything change. Let’s tweak your file a little bit more so that you can see the power of caching.

  3. Replace the line data_load_state.text('Loading data...done!') with this:

    Python
    data_load_state.text("Done! (using st.cache_data)")

  4. Now save. See how the line you added appeared immediately? If you take a step back for a second, this is actually quite amazing. Something magical is happening behind the scenes, and it only takes one line of code to activate it.
How's it work?
Let's take a few minutes to discuss how @st.cache_data actually works.
When you mark a function with Streamlit’s cache annotation, it tells Streamlit that whenever the function is called that it should check two things:

1. The input parameters you used for the function call.
  2. The code inside the function.

If this is the first time Streamlit has seen both these items, with these exact values, and in this exact combination, it runs the function and stores the result in a local cache. The next time the function is called, if the two values haven't changed, then Streamlit knows it can skip executing the function altogether. Instead, it reads the output from the local cache and passes it on to the caller -- like magic.
"But, wait a second," you’re saying to yourself, "this sounds too good to be true. What are the limitations of all this awesomesauce?"
Well, there are a few:

1. Streamlit will only check for changes within the current working directory. If you upgrade a Python library, Streamlit's cache will only notice this if that library is installed inside your working directory.
  2. If your function is not deterministic (that is, its output depends on random numbers), or if it pulls data from an external time-varying source (for example, a live stock market ticker service) the cached value will be none-the-wiser.
  3. Lastly, you should avoid mutating the output of a function cached with st.cache_data since cached values are stored by reference.
While these limitations are important to keep in mind, they tend not to be an issue a surprising amount of the time. Those times, this cache is really transformational.

star

Tip

Whenever you have a long-running computation in your code, consider refactoring it so you can use @st.cache_data, if possible. Please read Caching for more details.
Now that you know how caching with Streamlit works, let’s get back to the Uber pickup data.
Inspect the raw data
It's always a good idea to take a look at the raw data you're working with before you start working with it. Let's add a subheader and a printout of the raw data to the app:

Python
st.subheader('Raw data')
st.write(data)
In the Basic concepts guide you learned that st.write will render almost anything you pass to it. In this case, you're passing in a dataframe and it's rendering as an interactive table.

st.write tries to do the right thing based on the data type of the input. If it isn't doing what you expect you can use a specialized command like st.dataframe instead. For a full list, see API reference.
Draw a histogram
Now that you've had a chance to take a look at the dataset and observe what's available, let's take things a step further and draw a histogram to see what Uber's busiest hours are in New York City.

1. To start, let's add a subheader just below the raw data section:

    Python
    st.subheader('Number of pickups by hour')

  2. Use NumPy to generate a histogram that breaks down pickup times binned by hour:

    Python
    hist_values = np.histogram(
    data[DATE_COLUMN].dt.hour, bins=24, range=(0,24))[0]

  3. Now, let's use Streamlit's st.bar_chart() method to draw this histogram.

    Python
    st.bar_chart(hist_values)

  4. Save your script. This histogram should show up in your app right away. After a quick review, it looks like the busiest time is 17:00 (5 P.M.).

To draw this diagram we used Streamlit's native bar_chart() method, but it's important to know that Streamlit supports more complex charting libraries like Altair, Bokeh, Plotly, Matplotlib and more. For a full list, see supported charting libraries.
Plot data on a map

Using a histogram with Uber's dataset helped us determine what the busiest times are for pickups, but what if we wanted to figure out where pickups were concentrated throughout the city. While you could use a bar chart to show this data, it wouldn't be easy to interpret unless you were intimately familiar with latitudinal and longitudinal coordinates in the city. To show pickup concentration, let's use Streamlit st.map() function to overlay the data on a map of New York City.

1. Add a subheader for the section:

    Python
    st.subheader('Map of all pickups')

  2. Use the st.map() function to plot the data:

    Python
    st.map(data)

  3. Save your script. The map is fully interactive. Give it a try by panning or zooming in a bit.
After drawing your histogram, you determined that the busiest hour for Uber pickups was 17:00. Let's redraw the map to show the concentration of pickups at 17:00.

1. Locate the following code snippet:

    Python
    st.subheader('Map of all pickups')
st.map(data)

  2. Replace it with:

    Python
    hour_to_filter = 17
filtered_data = data[data[DATE_COLUMN].dt.hour == hour_to_filter]
st.subheader(f'Map of all pickups at {hour_to_filter}:00')
st.map(filtered_data)

  3. You should see the data update instantly.
To draw this map we used the st.map function that's built into Streamlit, but if you'd like to visualize complex map data, we encourage you to take a look at the st.pydeck_chart.
Filter results with a slider

In the last section, when you drew the map, the time used to filter results was hardcoded into the script, but what if we wanted to let a reader dynamically filter the data in real time? Using Streamlit's widgets you can. Let's add a slider to the app with the st.slider() method.

1. Locate hour_to_filter and replace it with this code snippet:

    Python
    hour_to_filter = st.slider('hour', 0, 23, 17)  # min: 0h, max: 23h, default: 17h

  2. Use the slider and watch the map update in real time.
Use a button to toggle data

Sliders are just one way to dynamically change the composition of your app. Let's use the st.checkbox function to add a checkbox to your app. We'll use this checkbox to show/hide the raw data table at the top of your app.

1. Locate these lines:

    Python
    st.subheader('Raw data')
st.write(data)

  2. Replace these lines with the following code:

    Python
    if st.checkbox('Show raw data'):
    st.subheader('Raw data')
    st.write(data)
We're sure you've got your own ideas. When you're done with this tutorial, check out all the widgets that Streamlit exposes in our API Reference.
Let's put it all together
That's it, you've made it to the end. Here's the complete script for our interactive app.

star

Tip

If you've skipped ahead, after you've created your script, the command to run Streamlit is streamlit run [app name].

Python
import streamlit as st
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

st.title('Uber pickups in NYC')

DATE_COLUMN = 'date/time'
DATA_URL = ('https://s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com/'
            'streamlit-demo-data/uber-raw-data-sep14.csv.gz')

@st.cache_data
def load_data(nrows):
    data = pd.read_csv(DATA_URL, nrows=nrows)
    lowercase = lambda x: str(x).lower()
    data.rename(lowercase, axis='columns', inplace=True)
    data[DATE_COLUMN] = pd.to_datetime(data[DATE_COLUMN])
    return data

data_load_state = st.text('Loading data...')
data = load_data(10000)
data_load_state.text("Done! (using st.cache_data)")

if st.checkbox('Show raw data'):
    st.subheader('Raw data')
    st.write(data)

st.subheader('Number of pickups by hour')
hist_values = np.histogram(data[DATE_COLUMN].dt.hour, bins=24, range=(0,24))[0]
st.bar_chart(hist_values)

# Some number in the range 0-23
hour_to_filter = st.slider('hour', 0, 23, 17)
filtered_data = data[data[DATE_COLUMN].dt.hour == hour_to_filter]

st.subheader('Map of all pickups at %s:00' % hour_to_filter)
st.map(filtered_data)

blocks.html: 创建应用
读到这里，你可能已经安装了 Streamlit，并阅读了基础概念和进阶概念。如果还没有，现在正适合先看一看。
学习 Streamlit 最简单的方法，就是亲自动手。阅读本指南时，请逐个试用这些方法。只要应用正在运行，每次向脚本添加新元素并保存后，Streamlit 界面就会询问是否重新运行应用、查看变化。这样就能形成快速的交互循环：编写代码、保存、查看输出，再继续编写和调整，直到对结果满意。我们的目标是用 Streamlit 为你的数据或模型创建交互式应用，并在此过程中用它检查、调试、完善和分享代码。
本指南将使用 Streamlit 的核心功能创建一个交互式应用，探索纽约市 Uber 上下车记录的公开数据集。完成后，你将掌握获取与缓存数据、绘制图表、在地图上标记信息，以及通过滑块等交互组件筛选结果的方法。

★

提示

如果想直接跳到完整结果，下方提供了完整脚本.
创建第一个应用
Streamlit 不仅是创建数据应用的工具，也是创作者交流应用、分享想法并互相帮助改进作品的社区。欢迎加入社区论坛。我们期待听到你的问题和想法，也愿意帮助排查程序中的错误——现在就来看看吧！

1. 第一步，创建一个新的 Python 脚本。我们把它命名为 uber_pickups.py.

  2. 打开 uber_pickups.py，使用你喜欢的 IDE 或文本编辑器，加入以下代码：

    Python
    import streamlit as st
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

  3. 好的应用都需要标题，我们来添加一个：

    Python
    st.title('Uber pickups in NYC')

  4. 现在可以从命令行运行 Streamlit：

    终端
    streamlit run uber_pickups.py

    运行 Streamlit 应用与运行其他 Python 脚本类似。每次需要查看应用时，都可以使用这个命令。

    ★

    提示

    你知道吗？也可以向 streamlit run 传入 URL！与 GitHub Gists 配合使用尤其方便。例如：

    终端
    streamlit run https://raw.githubusercontent.com/streamlit/demo-uber-nyc-pickups/master/streamlit_app.py

  5. 和往常一样，应用应当会自动在浏览器的新标签页中打开。
获取数据
现在已经有了应用，接下来需要获取纽约市 Uber 上下车记录的数据集。

1. 先编写一个加载数据的函数。将以下代码加入脚本：

    Python
    DATE_COLUMN = 'date/time'
DATA_URL = ('https://s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com/'
         'streamlit-demo-data/uber-raw-data-sep14.csv.gz')

def load_data(nrows):
    data = pd.read_csv(DATA_URL, nrows=nrows)
    lowercase = lambda x: str(x).lower()
    data.rename(lowercase, axis='columns', inplace=True)
    data[DATE_COLUMN] = pd.to_datetime(data[DATE_COLUMN])
    return data

    你会发现，load_data 是一个普通函数：它下载数据，将其放入 Pandas 数据表，并把日期列从文本转换为日期时间类型。这个函数接收一个参数（nrows），用于指定加载到数据表中的行数。

  2. 现在测试函数并查看输出。在函数下面添加以下代码：

    Python
    # Create a text element and let the reader know the data is loading.
data_load_state = st.text('Loading data...')
# Load 10,000 rows of data into the dataframe.
data = load_data(10000)
# Notify the reader that the data was successfully loaded.
data_load_state.text('Loading data...done!')

    应用右上角会出现一些按钮，询问是否重新运行应用。选择 Always rerun（始终重新运行），之后每次保存都能自动看到变化。
好吧，效果似乎没有那么惊艳……
事实证明，下载数据并将 10,000 行记录加载进数据表需要不少时间，把日期列转换为日期时间类型也不快。你肯定不希望应用每次更新都重新加载数据——幸运的是，Streamlit 可以缓存数据。
轻松使用缓存

1. 尝试添加 @st.cache_data，将它放在 load_data 声明之前：

    Python
    @st.cache_data
def load_data(nrows):

  2. 接着保存脚本，Streamlit 会自动重新运行应用。因为这是首次使用 @st.cache_data 运行脚本，所以暂时看不出变化。我们再稍微调整文件，让你看到缓存的作用。

  3. 把这一行 data_load_state.text('Loading data...done!') 替换为：

    Python
    data_load_state.text("Done! (using st.cache_data)")

  4. 现在保存。看到了吗，新增的文字立即出现了！退后一步想想，这确实很了不起：后台发生了一些神奇的事情，而你只用了一行代码就启用了它。
它是如何工作的？
我们花几分钟讨论 @st.cache_data 的实际工作方式。
给函数添加 Streamlit 缓存注解后，每次调用该函数，Streamlit 都会检查两项内容：

1. 调用函数时使用的输入参数。
  2. 函数内部的代码。
如果 Streamlit 第一次遇到这两项内容以这些确定的值、这种组合出现，就会执行函数，并把结果存入本地缓存。下次调用时，如果两项内容都没有变化，Streamlit 就知道可以完全跳过函数执行，直接从本地缓存读取输出并返回给调用方——就像魔法一样。
你可能会想：“等一下，这听起来好得让人难以置信。它究竟有什么限制？”
确实有几个限制：

1. Streamlit 只会检查当前工作目录内的变化。如果升级了某个 Python 库，只有该库安装在工作目录中，Streamlit 的缓存才会注意到这一变化。
  2. 如果函数不是确定性的（例如输出依赖随机数），或者从外部获取随时间变化的数据（例如实时股票行情服务），缓存并不会自动知道这些变化。
  3. 最后，应当避免修改由 st.cache_data 缓存的函数输出，因为缓存值是按引用保存的。
虽然需要注意这些限制，但在很多情况下，它们都不会成为问题。这时，缓存会带来非常显著的改善。

★

提示

如果代码中有耗时计算，可以考虑调整其组织方式，以便尽可能使用 @st.cache_data。更多细节请阅读缓存专题。
了解了 Streamlit 缓存的工作方式后，我们继续处理 Uber 上车记录。
查看原始数据
先查看原始数据通常是个好习惯。我们给应用添加一个小标题，并显示原始数据：

Python
st.subheader('Raw data')
st.write(data)
在基础概念指南中，你已经了解到 st.write 几乎可以渲染任何传入的内容。这里传入的是数据表，因此它会被渲染为交互式表格。
st.write 会根据输入的数据类型，尽量选择合适的展示方式。如果结果不符合预期，可以改用更具体的命令，例如 st.dataframe。完整列表请参阅API 参考.
绘制直方图
查看数据集并了解其内容后，我们再进一步，绘制直方图，看看纽约市 Uber 上车最繁忙的时段。

1. 首先，在原始数据部分下方添加一个小标题：

    Python
    st.subheader('Number of pickups by hour')

  2. 用 NumPy 生成一个按小时分组的上车时间直方图：

    Python
    hist_values = np.histogram(
    data[DATE_COLUMN].dt.hour, bins=24, range=(0,24))[0]

  3. 然后，使用 Streamlit 的 st.bar_chart() 方法绘制该直方图。

    Python
    st.bar_chart(hist_values)

  4. 保存脚本，直方图应立即显示在应用中。简单查看后可以发现，最繁忙的时间是 17:00，也就是下午 5 点。
这张图使用了 Streamlit 原生的 bar_chart() 方法，不过 Streamlit 也支持 Altair、Bokeh、Plotly、Matplotlib 等更复杂的图表库。完整列表请参阅支持的图表库.
在地图上绘制数据
Uber 数据的直方图让我们找到了最繁忙的上车时段，但如果想知道这些上车点集中在城市的哪些地方呢？虽然也可以用柱状图展示，但除非十分熟悉城市的经纬度，否则不容易理解。为了展示上车点的空间分布，我们使用 Streamlit 的 st.map() 函数，把数据叠加到纽约市地图上。

1. 给这一部分添加一个小标题：

    Python
    st.subheader('Map of all pickups')

  2. 使用 st.map() 函数绘制数据：

    Python
    st.map(data)

  3. 保存脚本。这张地图可以交互，试着拖动或缩放一下。
前面的直方图表明，Uber 最繁忙的上车时段是 17:00。接下来重新绘制地图，只显示 17:00 上车点的分布。

1. 找到以下代码片段：

    Python
    st.subheader('Map of all pickups')
st.map(data)

  2. 将其替换为：

    Python
    hour_to_filter = 17
filtered_data = data[data[DATE_COLUMN].dt.hour == hour_to_filter]
st.subheader(f'Map of all pickups at {hour_to_filter}:00')
st.map(filtered_data)

  3. 你应当能立即看到数据更新。
绘制这张地图时，我们使用了 Streamlit 内置的 st.map 函数。如果希望可视化更复杂的地图数据，建议进一步了解 st.pydeck_chart.
使用滑块筛选结果
上一节绘制地图时，筛选数据所用的时间被直接写在脚本中。如果希望读者实时选择筛选条件呢？Streamlit 的交互组件可以做到。我们用 st.slider() 方法给应用添加一个滑块。

1. 找到 hour_to_filter，将其替换为下面的代码：

    Python
    hour_to_filter = st.slider('hour', 0, 23, 17)  # min: 0h, max: 23h, default: 17h

  2. 操作滑块，观察地图如何实时更新。
使用按钮切换数据显示
滑块只是动态改变应用内容的一种方式。我们使用 st.checkbox 函数再添加一个复选框，用它显示或隐藏应用顶部的原始数据表。

1. 找到以下代码行：

    Python
    st.subheader('Raw data')
st.write(data)

  2. 将它们替换为以下代码：

    Python
    if st.checkbox('Show raw data'):
    st.subheader('Raw data')
    st.write(data)
相信你已经有了自己的想法。完成本教程后，可以查看 Streamlit 提供的全部交互组件，详见API 参考.
把所有内容组合起来
到这里，你已经完成了整个流程！下面是交互式应用的完整脚本。

★

提示

如果你直接跳到了这里，创建脚本后，运行 Streamlit 的命令是 streamlit run [app name].

Python
import streamlit as st
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

st.title('Uber pickups in NYC')

DATE_COLUMN = 'date/time'
DATA_URL = ('https://s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com/'
            'streamlit-demo-data/uber-raw-data-sep14.csv.gz')

@st.cache_data
def load_data(nrows):
    data = pd.read_csv(DATA_URL, nrows=nrows)
    lowercase = lambda x: str(x).lower()
    data.rename(lowercase, axis='columns', inplace=True)
    data[DATE_COLUMN] = pd.to_datetime(data[DATE_COLUMN])
    return data

data_load_state = st.text('Loading data...')
data = load_data(10000)
data_load_state.text("Done! (using st.cache_data)")

if st.checkbox('Show raw data'):
    st.subheader('Raw data')
    st.write(data)

st.subheader('Number of pickups by hour')
hist_values = np.histogram(data[DATE_COLUMN].dt.hour, bins=24, range=(0,24))[0]
st.bar_chart(hist_values)

# Some number in the range 0-23
hour_to_filter = st.slider('hour', 0, 23, 17)
filtered_data = data[data[DATE_COLUMN].dt.hour == hour_to_filter]

st.subheader('Map of all pickups at %s:00' % hour_to_filter)
st.map(filtered_data)
分享应用
构建好 Streamlit 应用后，就可以分享它了！要向大家展示，可以使用 Streamlit Community Cloud 免费部署、管理并分享应用。
只需三个简单步骤：

1. 把应用放入公开的 GitHub 仓库，并确保仓库中包含 requirements.txt！
  2. 登录 share.streamlit.io
  3. 点击“Deploy an app”（部署应用），然后粘贴 GitHub URL。
完成！🎈 现在你有了公开部署的应用，可以分享给所有人。点击链接，进一步了解如何使用 Streamlit Community Cloud.
获取帮助
入门内容到这里就结束了，你可以开始构建自己的应用了！如果遇到困难，可以尝试以下方式：

• 访问我们的社区论坛并发布问题。
  • 通过命令行获取快速帮助：streamlit help

st.write

Displays arguments in the app.

This is the Swiss Army knife of Streamlit commands: it does different things depending on what you throw at it. Unlike other Streamlit commands, st.write() has some unique properties:

  • You can pass in multiple arguments, all of which will be displayed.
  • Its behavior depends on the input type(s).
Function signature[source]

st.write(*args, unsafe_allow_html=False)

Parameters

*args (any)

One or many objects to display in the app.

Each type of argument is handled as follows:
Type Handling
str Uses st.markdown().
dataframe-like, dict, or list Uses st.dataframe().
Exception Uses st.exception().
function, module, or class Uses st.help().
DeltaGenerator Uses st.help().
Altair chart Uses st.altair_chart().
Graphviz graph Uses st.graphviz_chart().
Keras model Converts model and uses st.graphviz_chart().
Matplotlib figure Uses st.pyplot().
Plotly figure Uses st.plotly_chart().

An object with ._repr_html() Uses st.html().

Any Displays str(arg) as inline code.

Whether to render HTML within *args. This only applies to strings or objects falling back on _repr_html_(). If this is False (default), any HTML tags found in body will be escaped and therefore treated as raw text. If this is True, any HTML expressions within body will be rendered.

st.button

Display a button widget.

Function signature[source]

st.button(label, key=None, help=None, on_click=None, args=None, kwargs=None, *, type="secondary", icon=None, icon_position="left", disabled=False, use_container_width=None, width="content", shortcut=None, wrap=None)

Parameters

label (str)

A short label explaining to the user what this button is for. The label can optionally contain GitHub-flavored Markdown of the following types: Bold, Italics, Strikethroughs, Inline Code, Links, and Images. Images display like icons, with a max height equal to the font height.

Unsupported Markdown elements are unwrapped so only their children (text contents) render. Common block-level Markdown (headings, lists, blockquotes) is automatically escaped and displays as literal text in labels.

See the body parameter of st.markdown for additional, supported Markdown directives.

key (str, int, or None)

An optional string or integer to use as the unique key for the widget. If this is None (default), a key will be generated for the widget based on the values of the other parameters. No two widgets may have the same key. Assigning a key stabilizes the widget's identity and preserves its state across reruns even when other parameters change.

A key lets you access the widget's value via st.session_state[key] (read-only). For more details, see Widget behavior.

Additionally, if key is provided, it will be used as a CSS class name prefixed with st-key-.

help (str or None)

A tooltip that gets displayed when the button is hovered over. If this is None (default), no tooltip is displayed.

The tooltip can optionally contain GitHub-flavored Markdown, including the Markdown directives described in the body parameter of st.markdown.

on_click (callable)

An optional callback invoked when this button is clicked.

args (list or tuple)

An optional list or tuple of args to pass to the callback.

kwargs (dict)

An optional dict of kwargs to pass to the callback.

type ("primary", "secondary", or "tertiary")

An optional string that specifies the button type. This can be one of the following:

  • "primary": The button's background is the app's primary color for additional emphasis.
  • "secondary" (default): The button's background coordinates with the app's background color for normal emphasis.
  • "tertiary": The button is plain text without a border or background for subtlety.

icon (str or None)

An optional emoji or icon to display next to the button label. If icon is None (default), no icon is displayed. If icon is a string, the following options are valid:

  • A single-character emoji. For example, you can set icon="🚨" or icon="🔥". Emoji short codes are not supported.

  • An icon from the Material Symbols library (rounded style) in the format ":material/icon_name:" where "icon_name" is the name of the icon in snake case.

    For example, icon=":material/thumb_up:" will display the Thumb Up icon. Find additional icons in the Material Symbols font library.

  • "spinner": Displays a spinner as an icon.

icon_position ("left" or "right")

The position of the icon relative to the button label. This defaults to "left".

disabled (bool)

An optional boolean that disables the button if set to True. The default is False.

use_container_width (bool)

use_container_width is deprecated and will be removed in a future release. For use_container_width=True, use width="stretch". For use_container_width=False, use width="content".

Whether to expand the button's width to fill its parent container. If use_container_width is False (default), Streamlit sizes the button to fit its contents. If use_container_width is True, the width of the button matches its parent container.

In both cases, if the contents of the button are wider than the parent container, the contents will line wrap.

width ("content", "stretch", or int)

The width of the button. This can be one of the following:

  • "content" (default): The width of the button matches the width of its content, but doesn't exceed the width of the parent container.
  • "stretch": The width of the button matches the width of the parent container.
  • An integer specifying the width in pixels: The button has a fixed width. If the specified width is greater than the width of the parent container, the width of the button matches the width of the parent container.

shortcut (str or None)

An optional keyboard shortcut that triggers the button. This can be one of the following strings:

  • A single alphanumeric key like "K" or "4".
  • A function key like "F11".
  • A special key like "Enter", "Esc", or "Tab".
  • Any of the above combined with modifiers. For example, you can use "Ctrl+K" or "Cmd+Shift+O".

Important

The keys "C" and "R" are reserved and can't be used, even with modifiers. Punctuation keys like "." and "," aren't currently supported. Some combinations such as "Ctrl+T", "Ctrl+W", "Ctrl+PageUp", "Ctrl+PageDown", and "F11" are reserved by the browser or operating system and may never reach Streamlit.

The following special keys are supported: Backspace, Delete, Down, End, Enter, Esc, Home, Left, PageDown, PageUp, Right, Space, Tab, and Up.

The following modifiers are supported: Alt, Ctrl, Cmd, Meta, Mod, Option, Shift.

  • Ctrl, Cmd, Meta, and Mod are interchangeable and will display to the user to match their platform.
  • Option and Alt are interchangeable and will display to the user to match their platform.

wrap (bool or None)

Whether the button label can wrap onto multiple lines. This can be one of the following:

  • None (default): Streamlit decides based on the surrounding layout. Inside a horizontal container or when directly placed in a column (not nested in another container), the button keeps its standard, single-row height and truncates an overflowing label with an ellipsis; in other layouts, the label wraps onto additional lines.
  • True: If the label is too wide for the button, it wraps onto additional lines and the button grows taller.
  • False: The button keeps its standard, single-row height. A label that is too wide is truncated with an ellipsis.

When a single-row label is truncated with an ellipsis and no help is set, hovering reveals the full label. Icons and keyboard shortcuts remain visible.

Returns

(bool)

True if the button was clicked on the last run of the app, False otherwise.

Examples

Example 1: Customize your button type

import streamlit as st

st.button("Reset", type="primary")
if st.button("Say hello"):
    st.write("Why hello there")
else:
    st.write("Goodbye")

if st.button("Aloha", type="tertiary"):
    st.write("Ciao")
Interactive demo (opens online)
Built with Streamlit 🎈
Fullscreen open_in_new

Example 2: Add icons to your button

Although you can add icons to your buttons through Markdown, the icon parameter is a convenient and consistent alternative.

import streamlit as st

left, middle, right = st.columns(3)
if left.button("Plain button", width="stretch"):
    left.markdown("You clicked the plain button.")
if middle.button("Emoji button", icon="😃", width="stretch"):
    middle.markdown("You clicked the emoji button.")
if right.button("Material button", icon=":material/mood:", width="stretch"):
    right.markdown("You clicked the Material button.")
Interactive demo (opens online)
Built with Streamlit 🎈
Fullscreen open_in_new

Example 3: Use keyboard shortcuts

The following example shows how to use keyboard shortcuts to trigger a button. If you use any of the platform-dependent modifiers (Ctrl, Cmd, or Mod), they are interpreted interchangeably and always displayed to the user to match their platform.

import streamlit as st

with st.container(horizontal=True, horizontal_alignment="distribute"):
    "`A`" if st.button("A", shortcut="A") else "` `"
    "`S`" if st.button("S", shortcut="Ctrl+S") else "` `"
    "`D`" if st.button("D", shortcut="Cmd+Shift+D") else "` `"
    "`F`" if st.button("F", shortcut="Mod+Alt+Shift+F") else "` `"

st.button

显示一个按钮交互组件。

函数签名[源代码]

st.button(label, key=None, help=None, on_click=None, args=None, kwargs=None, *, type="secondary", icon=None, icon_position="left", disabled=False, use_container_width=None, width="content", shortcut=None, wrap=None)

参数

label （字符串）

简短标签，用来向用户说明按钮的用途。标签可包含以下 GitHub 风格 Markdown：粗体、斜体、删除线、行内代码、链接和图片。图片会像图标一样显示，最大高度等于字体高度。

不支持的 Markdown 元素会被去除外层标记，仅保留其中的文本。标题、列表、引用等常见块级 Markdown 会被自动转义，并在标签中显示为原始文本。

关于 body 参数所支持的其他 Markdown 指令，请参阅 st.markdown。

key （字符串、整数或 None）

可选的字符串或整数，用作该交互组件的唯一键。如果设置为 None（默认），系统会根据其他参数的值生成一个键。两个组件不能使用相同的键。指定 key 可以稳定组件身份，即使其他参数变化，也能在重新运行时保留状态。

设置 key 后，可通过 st.session_state[key] 访问组件的值（只读）。更多细节请参阅交互组件的行为.

此外，如果提供了 key，它还会成为一个带有以下前缀的 CSS 类名：st-key-.

help （字符串或 None）

鼠标悬停在按钮上时显示的提示文字。如果设置为 None（默认），则不显示提示。

提示文字可包含 GitHub 风格 Markdown，包括 body 参数描述的指令；该参数属于 st.markdown.

on_click （可调用对象）

可选的回调函数，点击按钮时调用。

args （列表或元组）

可选的列表或元组，用来向回调函数传递位置参数。

kwargs （字典）

可选字典，用来向回调函数传递关键字参数。

type （"primary"、"secondary" 或 "tertiary"）

可选字符串，用于指定按钮类型，可取以下值：

  • "primary"：按钮背景采用应用主色，使其更加醒目。
  • "secondary"（默认）：按钮背景与应用背景协调，提供普通程度的强调。
  • "tertiary"：按钮显示为纯文本，没有边框或背景，视觉上更轻。

icon （字符串或 None）

可选的表情或图标，显示在按钮标签旁。如果 icon 为 None（默认），则不显示图标。如果 icon 是字符串，可使用以下选项：

  • 单个字符的表情。例如，可以设置 icon="🚨" 或 icon="🔥"。不支持表情短代码。

  • Material Symbols 图标库中的圆角样式图标，格式为 ":material/icon_name:"，其中“icon_name”是采用下划线命名法的图标名称。

    例如，icon=":material/thumb_up:" 会显示点赞图标。更多图标请查阅 Material Symbols 字体库。

  • "spinner"：显示加载旋转指示器。

icon_position （"left" 或 "right"）

图标相对于按钮标签的位置，默认是 "left".

disabled （布尔值）

可选布尔值。设置为 True 时禁用按钮。默认值为 False.

use_container_width （布尔值）

use_container_width 已弃用，将在未来版本中移除。对于 use_container_width=True，请使用 width="stretch"。对于 use_container_width=False，请使用 width="content".

是否扩展按钮宽度以填满父容器。如果 use_container_width 为 False（默认），Streamlit 会按内容调整按钮宽度。如果 use_container_width 为 True，按钮宽度会与父容器一致。

无论哪种情况，当按钮内容宽于父容器时，内容都会换行。

width （"content"、"stretch" 或整数）

按钮宽度，可以使用以下值：

  • "content"（默认）：按钮宽度与内容宽度一致，但不超过父容器宽度。
  • "stretch"：按钮宽度与父容器宽度一致。
  • 用整数指定像素宽度：按钮具有固定宽度。如果指定宽度大于父容器宽度，按钮会改为与父容器等宽。

shortcut （字符串或 None）

可选的键盘快捷键，用于触发按钮。可使用以下字符串：

  • 单个字母或数字键，例如 "K" 或 "4".
  • 功能键，例如 "F11".
  • 特殊键，例如 "Enter", "Esc" 或 "Tab".
  • 上述按键与修饰键的组合。例如，可以使用 "Ctrl+K" 或 "Cmd+Shift+O".

重要

按键 "C" 和 "R" 为保留键，即使加上修饰键也不能使用。目前也不支持以下标点键："." 和 ","。某些组合键，例如 "Ctrl+T", "Ctrl+W", "Ctrl+PageUp", "Ctrl+PageDown" 和 "F11"，由浏览器或操作系统保留，可能无法传递到 Streamlit。

支持的特殊键包括：Backspace、Delete、Down、End、Enter、Esc、Home、Left、PageDown、PageUp、Right、Space、Tab 和 Up。

支持的修饰键包括：Alt、Ctrl、Cmd、Meta、Mod、Option 和 Shift。

  • Ctrl、Cmd、Meta 和 Mod 可互换使用，显示给用户时会匹配其所在平台。
  • Option 和 Alt 可互换使用，显示给用户时会匹配其所在平台。

wrap （布尔值或 None）

是否允许按钮标签换成多行，可以使用以下值：

  • None（默认）：Streamlit 根据周围布局决定。在水平容器中，或直接位于一列中且未嵌套于其他容器时，按钮维持标准的单行高度，超长标签用省略号截断；其他布局中，标签会换行显示。
  • True：如果标签太宽，就换成多行，按钮相应增高。
  • False：按钮保持标准单行高度；标签太宽时用省略号截断。

单行标签被省略号截断，且未设置 help 时，鼠标悬停会显示完整标签。图标和键盘快捷键始终可见。

返回值

（布尔值）

如果按钮在应用上一次运行时被点击，则返回 True；否则返回 False。

示例

示例 1：自定义按钮类型

import streamlit as st

st.button("Reset", type="primary")
if st.button("Say hello"):
    st.write("Why hello there")
else:
    st.write("Goodbye")

if st.button("Aloha", type="tertiary"):
    st.write("Ciao")

left, middle, right = st.columns(3)
if left.button("Plain button", width="stretch"):
    left.markdown("You clicked the plain button.")
if middle.button("Emoji button", icon="😃", width="stretch"):
    middle.markdown("You clicked the emoji button.")

示例 3：使用键盘快捷键

with st.container(horizontal=True, horizontal_alignment="distribute"):
    "`A`" if st.button("A", shortcut="A") else "` `"
    "`S`" if st.button("S", shortcut="Ctrl+S") else "` `"
    "`D`" if st.button("D", shortcut="Cmd+Shift+D") else "` `"
    "`F`" if st.button("F", shortcut="Mod+Alt+Shift+F") else "` `"
